The Axios compromise isn't a one-off. This has been the dominant attack pattern in the JavaScript ecosystem for the past year:
— stolen publishing token via GitHub Actions
— maintainer phished via fake npmjs.help domain
— stolen maintainer token, RAT via postinstall
Notice the pattern: stolen credentials → malicious publish → postinstall payload → your machine is compromised. Same playbook every time.
Ok, scary stuff. But this is fixable. Here's what to set up — it takes about 5 minutes and you only do it once.
Socket is the company that caught the Axios attack in 6 minutes. They make a free tool called
(Socket Firewall) that acts as a security proxy between npm and the package registry. Every package gets checked against Socket's malware database

# Socket Firewall — npm supply chain protection
alias npm="sfw npm"
alias npx="sfw npx"
That's it. No account, no API key, no config files. From now on, every
checks packages against Socket's database first. If it finds known malware, the install is blocked. If it detects something suspicious but unconfirmed, you get a warning.
